item.description:
Themes made in Lokyr: a Theme Editor of every color of a theme, its values edited of a field or of the system's color panel and written into the theme's file, its comments kept; themes made, duplicated, converted and imported in the app; and the settings' Keys page.
## What's new since 1.1.0
- **The Theme Editor**: on the settings window's Themes page, the Editor shows every color of a theme, the terminal's and the interface's by groups, each of its value and where it comes from: the theme's file and its line, a theme that it extends, or a rule. A click on a color opens a field of its value, a color, or for an interface color an expression of other colors, as `accent / 40%`, written into the theme's file as you pause or press Return; a click on its swatch opens the system's color panel, the eyedropper too, the color showing at once as you move. Reset puts a color back as it was when the Editor showed the theme. - **Previews of the theme edited**: beside the colors, a window of the theme, its tab bar, a scroll bar, a second pane and a terminal of every combination that it colors, and a plugin's panel of real controls, fields, toggles, a segmented control, a list, progresses and buttons, which take the pointer. A click on a part marks the colors that it takes, and a color's click the parts that take it. Your terminals keep their theme while the Editor shows another, and follow your edits of the theme that they use. - **Themes made in the app**: New… on the Themes page makes a theme of Lokyr's own light or dark values, every key written; Duplicate… in a card's menu copies a theme; View › New Theme from Current… copies the theme in use; View › Import Themes… imports `.itermcolors` and `.toml` themes, several at once. A theme of the collection or a built-in one is read-only in the Editor, whose lock makes a copy of it; an `.itermcolors` theme is converted to Lokyr's format as you edit it, its original moved to the Trash. - **The interface's colors follow the theme**: a theme's accent colors the focus ring, the selected rows, the toggles, the progress and the gutter of running commands, and its text the fainter texts, unless it gives them too; a color can be an expression of others, as `mix(background, foreground, 8%)`. A theme of the terminal's colors alone looks as it did. - **A light theme for both appearances**: a click on a theme of the appearance not in force asks whether to use it for its appearance alone or for both. - **The cursor guide**, a band across the cursor's row, as iTerm2's: View › Show Cursor Guide, ⌥⌘;, or `[cursor] guide`. - **Faint text** of its own opacity, `[text] faint-opacity`, and an **HDR cursor**, brighter than white on a display of extended dynamic range, `[cursor] hdr`, off by default. - **The Keys page**: the settings' shortcuts on a page of their own, of a field that filters them by their commands, their keys or their contexts. - **Window › Cycle Through Windows**, ⌘`, and ⇧⌘` the other way, the settings window among them. - **Plugins**: the plugin API 0.1.4 reads every color of a theme as it resolves, shows the system's color panel, asks a question of buttons, and draws a part of a view in a theme of a name.
## Changed
- The settings window has a theme of its own, Lokyr Light or Lokyr Dark by the appearance, whatever theme your terminals use. - What a theme colors nothing with no longer refuses it: a value that does not read, a name of no color or colors that name each other are told in the card, of their line, the rest of the theme in force. - A plugin's question names the plugin in its alert, unless it is one of Lokyr's own, and a plugin asks one question at a time. - The settings window draws anew faster, the Keys page above all, and Lokyr starts a little sooner.
## Fixed
- A saved theme that changes the interface's colors alone colors the tab bar, the panels and the settings window at once. - A block cursor on the cursor guide's row keeps its own color. - A resize no longer clears a running command's output of a shell whose prompt marks its start alone. - A pane that takes the keyboard, as Go to Next Agent brings it forward, ends its tab's zoom of another. - A right click or a ⌘-click on a path of a volume that does not answer, as a network's, no longer holds Lokyr. - A binding of a character that the US layout types with Shift, as `cmd+}`, runs as its keys are pressed and takes the place of a default of them; two entries of the same keys written two ways read, the later holding, where the whole config was refused. - `sleip check` refuses a plugin's config schema larger than 64 KiB, the most that Lokyr reads of one.
## Before you update
- Plugins installed for 1.1.0 keep working: the plugin API is 0.1.4, which takes 0.1.3's plugins. - Your settings window now shows Lokyr's own colors rather than your theme's.

Lokyr's settings, in a window of their own: every key of the config, the keys' bindings, the themes and the plugins, changed without editing a file, the config file staying yours, its comments kept.
## What's new since 1.0.0
- **The settings window**: Lokyr › Open Settings Window, or the command palette, opens the settings in a window of their own, of the size of System Settings', its pages as tabs across the top: Settings, Themes and Plugins. Settings…, ⌘,, still opens your config file. - **Every key of the config**: the Settings page lists every key of the config and of the bundled plugins' sections, by section in a sidebar, each of what it does, its value and a More info link to its text in the config guide. A toggle, a menu or a field changes a key at once, written into your `config.toml` as typing pauses, its comments kept; Reset takes a key back to its default, and a value that a key does not take says why. A search field finds the keys, the sections and the bindings by their words. - **Fonts, previewed**: a font's family and its styles are picked from menus of the system's fonts, the panes showing each one as its item rests highlighted, until the menu closes; a family chosen comments out the styles of your config that it lacks. - **Your shortcuts**: the Keys part lists every binding, Lokyr's defaults and yours, by category. A click on a binding's keys records the shortcut that you press next; Remove and Restore take a default away and give it back; Add records a new shortcut and offers every command by category. A shortcut that another binding takes says which, and macOS's own, as ⌘Q, stay as they are. - **Themes, at a glance**: the Themes page shows every theme, the built-in ones, the collection's and yours, as a sample terminal in its colors, the light and the dark ones apart; a click uses one for its appearance. - **Plugins, without the command line**: Lokyr › Plugins… lists every plugin, with its state and its capabilities, to disable, enable, update or remove; and the registry's plugins, to install without restarting. - **View › Open Themes Folder** opens the folder of your own themes in the Finder, making it first if it is not there. - **Plugins**: the plugin API 0.1.3 lets a plugin show a notice in Lokyr's card, of an icon of its level, as info, success, warning or error, and show a theme's preview in its views.
## Changed
- The config's texts have bounds: a name, as a font's family or a theme's, 256 characters at most, a path or an address 1024; a longer one is an error at its line.
## Fixed
- With the tab bar out of the titlebar and two tabs or more, the window's title stands centred and no longer lies over the plugins' buttons beside the window's buttons. - A single tab's title in the titlebar is the window's title, in the system title's look, and dims as the window loses the focus. - Choosing in a font picker the family that the config names already, after previewing another, shows it again. - A file of the themes' folder that is no regular file, or of more than 1 MiB, or an `.itermcolors` file whose property list nests or repeats its values past what a color preset holds, is refused as a theme that does not read, where it could hold Lokyr or make it quit.
## Before you update
- Plugins installed for 1.0.0 keep working: the plugin API is 0.1.3, which takes 0.1.2's plugins.

The first public release. Lokyr's source is open, under the MIT License, at [github.com/sephiroth74/lokyr](https://github.com/sephiroth74/lokyr), and [lokyr.dev](https://lokyr.dev) documents it. Lokyr installs from this disk image, or with Homebrew, `brew install --cask sephiroth74/tap/lokyr`, and updates itself.
## What's new since 0.9.0
- **AI agents on their tabs**: a tab running Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Aider or another agent that `[agents] programs` lists shows whether the agent works, waits for you, or is done with what you asked. What it asked shows in the tab's tooltip, as "Claude needs your permission to use Bash", and in a tab of several panes a ring goes round the pane that waits. - **Agents that wait for you**: a notification tells when an agent waits or is done while its window has no focus, and the Dock's icon counts the agents that wait. Window › Go to Next Agent, ⌥⌘A, brings the next one forward, across every window; Window › Show Agents…, ⇧⌥⌘A, lists them all in the palette, the most urgent first. - **Claude Code's integration**: Lokyr › Install Claude Code Integration… adds hooks to Claude Code's settings, asking of each of its configurations and keeping a copy of the file, so that Claude Code tells its tab exactly when it works, waits for you, is done, or stops on an error. - **A path opened at its line**: ⌘-click on a path's line, as `src/main.rs:42:7` that compilers, tests and agents print, opens the file at that line in the editor that `[links] editor` names: VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Zed, Sublime Text, TextMate or an address of your own. - **A command's output**: Edit › Copy Command Output, ⌥⇧⌘C, and Select Command Output, ⇧⌘A, copy or select the output of the last command, or, from the pane's context menu, of the command under the pointer, without its prompt and its command line. - **Inline images**: programs show pictures in the terminal, as `imgcat` sends them, of iTerm2's protocol, and as `kitten icat`, `chafa`, `timg` and file managers' previews send them, of kitty's graphics protocol; the images scroll with their lines and stay within 64 MiB of memory, as `[terminal] image-memory` says. - **Homebrew**: `brew install --cask sephiroth74/tap/lokyr` installs Lokyr and links `lokyr` and `sleip`, leaving the updates to Lokyr's own. - **Plugins**: the plugin API 0.1.2 lets a plugin list the agents of every window and open a file at a line in the editor. - About Lokyr links to lokyr.dev.
## Changed
- The icon's variant that `[app] icon` chooses stays in the Dock after Lokyr quits. - A click on a notification, a program's, an agent's or a long command's, brings forward the pane that sent it, with its tab and its window.
## Fixed
- A tab no longer keeps the title of a program that ended, as the remote shell's after you leave `ssh`: the title from before comes back, unless your shell sets its own at its prompt. - An agent that a shell starts with `exec` no longer misses its first request for you. - `sleip add` tells a plugin kept at the version that `plugins.lock` holds, and that `sleip update` of it takes a newer one, rather than failing of an older Lokyr's version. - `sleip info` no longer counts a yanked version when it tells that this Lokyr takes none of a plugin's versions. - `sleip dev` checks again a plugin saved while it was linking it.
## Before you update
- Plugins installed for 0.9.0 keep working: the plugin API is 0.1.2, which takes 0.1.1's plugins. - From 1.0.0, Lokyr's versions follow semantic versioning.
